guideFindings.what: podman rm -f workspace-test took 10 s and printed 'StopSignal SIGTERM failed to stop container ... resorting to SIGKILL': the base entrypoint ignores SIGTERM. Harmless, but looks like an error to a first reader. docker rm -f uses SIGKILL and has no delay.
guideFindings.extra: Optionally add after the code block: 'Podman waits 10 seconds for the entrypoint to stop and then kills it; -t 0 skips the wait.' Docker: docker rm -f has no wait.

guideFindings.what: The Job ran on the custom image and reached Ready in about 18 s, but the default Expert (worker_base, tools.shell = []) has no shell tool. The agent searched its workspace, found none, and reported 'no shell-execution tool is bound ... NOT EXECUTED' for all three commands. A reader who follows the guide's claim that 'the agent's own shell does [have your tools]' and asks the default Expert to run a tool will see this and think the image is broken.
guideFindings.oldText: A Job's IDE terminal runs in a separate pod with the installation's image, so it doesn't have your tools; the agent's own shell does.
guideFindings.newText: A Job's IDE terminal runs in a separate pod with the installation's image, so it doesn't have your tools. The agent's own shell does, but only for an Expert that has the shell tool group; the default Expert has no shell tool, so a Job that is meant to run your tools needs an Expert with it.
guideFindings.extra: Needs the exact name of a shipped Expert that has the shell group (not verified here). Product note, not a guide bug: a Job that cannot use the custom image's tools completes with a low-confidence 'NOT EXECUTED' report instead of failing, so a try-it Job on a new image proves little unless the Expert has a shell.

guideFindings.what: The guide says 'workspace-<first 12 characters of the Job ID>'. The real pod was workspace-1ec4b61d-51f for Job 1ec4b61d-51fc-...: 12 characters of the ID including the hyphen. kubectl describe with 13 characters (workspace-1ec4b61d-51fc) returns NotFound. The guide is correct; the brief's '8 characters' is not.
guideFindings.oldText: kubectl describe pod workspace-<first 12 characters of the Job ID>
guideFindings.newText: kubectl describe pod workspace-<first 12 characters of the Job ID, hyphen included>
guideFindings.extra: For example Job 1ec4b61d-51fc-43b4-... has the pod workspace-1ec4b61d-51f. Optional clarification only.

guideFindings.what: podman push --digestfile worked and the echo printed localhost:5005/a4-guide-tools@sha256:d3ac9b48.... ${IMAGE%:*} strips the tag only when IMAGE has a tag; without a tag, a registry port (localhost:5005/name) would be cut. The guide's example always has a tag, so this is correct as written. On the local registry the guide's Podman commands needed --tls-verify=false on build (for the base pull) and push, exactly as step 4 says; podman run/exec/rm needed none.

Negative check: with ENTRYPOINT ["true"] appended, podman run -d then sleep 10 and podman inspect printed 'exited' (exit code 0), so the guide's check catches it. With CMD ["true"] the container stayed 'running': the base entrypoint ignores CMD. So the guide's rule is right for ENTRYPOINT and USER, but a CMD override doesn't break the base.
guideFindings.oldText:
- **Don't set `ENTRYPOINT`, `CMD` or `USER`.** The base's entrypoint runs as
  root, starts sshd and keeps the container running.
guideFindings.newText:
- **Don't set `ENTRYPOINT`, `CMD` or `USER`.** The base's entrypoint runs as
  root, starts sshd and keeps the container running. (The entrypoint ignores its arguments, so a `CMD` has no effect, but it can mislead whoever reads the Dockerfile.)
guideFindings.extra: Optional wording; the rule itself is safe.
